domain: Political Economy / Institutional Theory / Ideology Studies
topic_summary: Analysis of how free markets are naturalized as the default economic arrangement, examining whether this naturalization results from lapsed-alternative closure (original construction forgotten, leaving only naturalized appearance) or beneficiary-maintained engineered closure (active institutional work disguised as natural default). The kernel contest centers on whether 'the market is natural' operates as sedimented ideology or as continuously defended power structure.

key_entities: Neoliberal governance apparatus (state institutions redesigned to protect markets)
Market fundamentalism ideology (theoretical realism privileging schema over evidence)
Beneficiary class (those who gain from upward redistribution)
Surplus populations (those policed by imperialist violence)
Progressive policy advocates (structurally disadvantaged by naturalization)
key_tensions: Active construction vs. natural emergence (neoliberalism requires state intervention vs. market presented as spontaneous)
Engineered closure vs. lapsed closure (ongoing institutional work vs. forgotten origins)
Universal aspiration vs. particularist dependence (global market system vs. violence against surplus populations)
key_mechanisms: Encasement (institutional redesign to protect markets from democratic demands)
Theoretical realism (ideational scheme treated as more true than empirical evidence)
Naturalization feedback loop (market outcomes appear inevitable, reinforcing acquiescence)
Post-hoc justification (beneficiaries hide interventions, frame redistribution as natural)
key_absences: Measurement of institutional maintenance costs (how much state capacity is required to sustain 'natural' markets)
Genealogy of specific naturalizations (which market features were contested when, and how contestation was closed)

axiom_contradictions.basis: Lapsed closure requires that original construction be forgotten and maintenance minimal; engineered closure requires ongoing active institutional work and visible beneficiary defense. No single framework can hold both 'the naturalization is self-sustaining ideology' and 'the naturalization requires continuous state intervention' as simultaneously true.

omegas.description: No systematic measurement of institutional maintenance costs for 'natural' markets. If engineered_closure_reading is correct, these costs should be quantifiable and substantial. If lapsed_closure_reading is correct, costs should be minimal. Absence of measurement prevents empirical adjudication.

Missing genealogy of specific naturalizations—which market features were contested when, and how contestation was closed. Would reveal whether closure was engineered (traceable interventions) or lapsed (forgotten origins). Historical record may exist but is not surfaced in policy discourse.

Dual_operation_reading may collapse into engineered_closure_reading if ideological disguise is merely epiphenomenal rather than structurally load-bearing. If lapsed closure is only surface appearance with no independent causal force, then only engineered closure operates. Empirical test: does removing ideological naturalization reduce institutional maintenance costs?

The axiom contradiction between lapsed and engineered readings is declared based on logical incompatibility, but empirical reality may instantiate both through temporal or spatial separation (lapsed in some domains, engineered in others). If so, dual_operation_reading is not synthesis but domain partition.

Engineered_closure_reading requires beneficiaries to be identifiable as active defenders. If beneficiaries are diffuse or if defense is automated through institutional design, the reading may misattribute agency. Lapsed_closure_reading avoids this by not requiring identifiable defenders.
